security_findings.title: Unauthenticated public model and tool invocation
evidence: agent_service.py POST /invoke has no authentication
render.yaml binds both services to 0.0.0.0
no rate or concurrency limit exists
security_findings.impact: Model/provider quota abuse, prompt attack exposure, and denial of service
security_findings.remediation: Require authenticated authorization, quotas, bounded concurrency, deadlines, and safe deployment defaults

security_findings.title: No enforceable active-scan authorization or scope gate
evidence: kali attack-url accepts arbitrary URLs
natural-language requests can dispatch web_app_attack immediately
authorization is documented only in README.md
security_findings.impact: Accidental or model-directed scans of unauthorized or sensitive systems
security_findings.remediation: Centralize scope validation, allowlists, explicit acknowledgement, sensitive-range blocking, redirect revalidation, and audit events

security_findings.title: Model-produced intent lacks strict post-parse policy validation
evidence: red_team_assistant.py accepts any nonempty model action and copies URL/flags
security_findings.impact: Prompt injection can influence privileged tool selection and target scope
security_findings.remediation: Use typed enums/schema, independently derive privileges, and enforce approval/policy after parsing

security_findings.title: Caller-controlled URLs create SSRF-style reachability
evidence: registry health URLs are opened directly
OLLAMA_URL is arbitrary
Kali scans accept arbitrary hosts
security_findings.impact: Internal service, metadata, or cross-zone network access
security_findings.remediation: Restrict schemes and destinations; validate DNS/IP/redirects; block sensitive address classes

security_findings.title: Plaintext unmanaged report retention
evidence: full assessments are serialized to reports
event traces retain prompts, URLs, and result details
no retention or encryption exists
security_findings.impact: Leakage through local access, backup, support bundle, or accidental publication
security_findings.remediation: Run-scoped restrictive storage, retention/rotation, URL sanitization, stronger redaction, and safe-share export

security_findings.title: Unpinned and unaudited dependency supply chain
evidence: requirements.txt contains only langgraph>=0.2.60
no lockfile, hash pinning, audit config, or CI exists
security_findings.remediation: Adopt pyproject, lock/hash dependencies, and audit them in CI

security_findings.title: Unbounded thread-per-request model execution
evidence: services use ThreadingHTTPServer
model calls can remain active for long timeouts
only body size is bounded
security_findings.impact: Thread, memory, provider quota, and file descriptor exhaustion
security_findings.remediation: Use bounded workers, queues, backpressure, rate limits, and timeouts

security_findings.title: Dynamic target imports execute trusted code without sandboxing
evidence: scanner/attack_runner.py dynamically imports enrolled modules
security_findings.impact: Malicious or compromised target code runs with scanner privileges
security_findings.remediation: Treat targets as trusted, review enrollment, and isolate third-party targets behind a constrained process/RPC boundary

security_findings.title: Suppressed HTTP logs and inconsistent exception responses
evidence: both handlers override log_message with no output
unexpected target exceptions are not normalized by the handler
security_findings.impact: Weak forensic visibility and ambiguous dropped connections
security_findings.remediation: Add structured redacted logs, request IDs, latency/outcome metrics, and safe 5xx responses

security_findings.title: Transport security depends on loopback or external proxy
evidence: services speak plaintext HTTP
no TLS or trusted-proxy configuration is documented
security_findings.impact: Prompts/responses exposed if services are placed on an untrusted network without TLS
security_findings.remediation: Keep local services loopback-only and require a trusted TLS edge for deployment
